Instances have been reported of stale/expired sweets being sold to consumers posing potential health hazards.

In case of pre-packaged/pre- packed sweets, the 'Date of Manufacturing' and 'Best before Date' of the products must be mentioned on their labels as per the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011.

sentences.text:
Subject:
Directions regarding display of "Date of Manufacturing" and "Best Before Date" in case of Sweets- Reg.
Reference:- FSSAI Order of even No. dated 25.09.2020

. 
Sir/Madam, With reference to Order of even NO. dated 25.09.2020 on the above subject, it is clarifed that the said Order is applicable for Indian Sweets only and the FBOs are permitted to display the mandatory 'Best Before Date' and 'Date of Manufacturing' (voluntary and non-binding)
on the container/tray holding sweets at the outlet for sale in the local language also.
Rest of the conditions of the Order dated 25.09.2020 remain unchanged.
Issued with the approval of the  Competent Authority."
(bold in original)

3. The frst of the impugned orders dated February 24, 2020 was superseded by the subsequent order dated September 25, 2020; therefore, in view of 4-PIL(L)-4407-2020.docx such supersession,
the said order dated February 24, 2020 has no independent existence.
The challenge thereto is redundant.

4. The order dated September 25, 2020 while superseding the order dated February 24, 2020 dilutes its rigours, in that it is no longer mandatory for the sweet sellers to display the manufacturing dates of the non-packaged/loose sweets on the containers/trays and it is purely optional.
However, the "Best Before Date" has to be mandatorily displayed depending upon the nature of the product and the local conditions.

sentences.text:
the earlier order of September 25, 2020 would apply to Indian sweets only and that the essential and non-essential indications may be displayed on the container/tray holding sweets at the retail outlet for sale in the local language also.
5. Despite the order dated February 24, 2020 no longer being in existence for the present, the purpose for which the same was issued and was followed by the orders dated September 25 and 30,
4-PIL(L)-4407-2020.docx 2020 is evident from its frst two paragraphs. It was in public interest and to ensure food safety, given the fact that stale/expired sweets were being put up for sale and consumption, that the respondents required the relevant food business operators to comply with the requirements specifed in paragraph 3.
6.

According to Dr. Warunjikar, learned Advocate for the petitioner, it is not possible for the members of the petitioner to suggest the shelf life of diferent types of sweets that are prepared and therefore, they cannot follow the requirements of the impugned orders.

7. In Ground (G) of the PIL petition it is asserted that the members of the petitioner are not experts in the feld of deciding the best before date, furthermore, the life of goods would vary on the basis of storage and handling of the buyer.
8. The life of a particular type of sweet would invariably depend on the quality of ingredients used.
We have failed to comprehend as to who, other than the manufacturer, would know how long 4-PIL(L)-4407-2020.docx the sweet would retain its original favour.
The requirement is of display of the "Best Before Date", thereby giving an option to the purchaser/consumer to decide whether to proceed for purchase or not.

The requirement of display has been insisted upon, keeping in mind the interests of the purchaser/consumer, and we fnd no reason to interfere.
9.
It is pleaded in the PIL petition that the same is being fled in the interest of the consumers and the public at large.

However, having heard Dr. Warunjikar and on perusal of the orders impugned,
we are of the considered opinion that the petitioner seeks to undo what the respondent no.2 proposed to introduce for the beneft of the purchasers/consumers.
This PIL petition is mischievous seeking to assail a justifable executive action for oblique purposes and thus it warrants dismissal in limine with costs.
We order accordingly.

10. The petitioner shall bear costs assessed at Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) to be paid to the Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa, to be used 4-PIL(L)-4407-2020.docx for the purpose of Covid relief, within a month from date failing which the same shall be recovered as arrears of land revenue.
